subject: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B Comprehensive Permit
overview: The board continued its review of a proposed 350-unit multifamily development, focusing on peer review coordination, department head feedback, and fire safety requirements for wood-frame construction.

items.title: Remote Meeting Preamble
items.summary: The chair opened the meeting by citing the governor's extension of remote meeting provisions through March 2023.

items.title: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway Peer Review Update
items.summary: The board provided updates on the hiring of Tetra Tech and Davis Square Architects as peer review consultants for site, traffic, and design review. The consultants will begin a three-to-four-week review process once initial documentation and funding from the applicant are finalized.

items.title: Building Safety and Fire Protection Recommendations
items.summary: Building Commissioner Bill Forte recommended requiring a temporary construction sprinkler system and enhanced site security to mitigate fire risks associated with large-scale wood-frame construction. The applicant agreed to make their design team available for code discussions with the commissioner.

items.title: Community Development Board and Document Requests
items.summary: The board requested several missing documents, including an updated waiver list, a 2019 traffic impact assessment, shadow studies, and a transportation demand management plan. Discussion of substantive recommendations from the Community Development Board, such as reducing building height, was deferred until the next meeting.

items.title: Affordable Housing and Local Preference
items.summary: The board discussed implementing a 70% local preference policy and the administrative necessity of 'floating' affordable units to maintain compliance if tenants exceed income limits. The hearing was continued to January 25, 2023, at which point public comment will be opened.

items.title: Executive Session: 4B60 Mystic Valley Parkway Litigation
items.summary: The board entered an executive session to discuss litigation strategy regarding an appeal by Sidney Wolk against the board's grant of variances for a laboratory facility.
